newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS/WINTERTHUR WEIGHS IN AS INVESTMENT HEAVYWEIGHT.
newsitem.headline: CS/WINTERTHUR WEIGHS IN AS INVESTMENT HEAVYWEIGHT.

text.p: A planned merger between banking powerhouse Credit Suisse Group and major Swiss insurer Winterthur Group will create a behemoth in the asset management industry which itself is seeing stunning growth, analysts said.
"In the financial sector, funds and asset management are seen as the fastest-growing areas," said Franco Catanzaro, analyst at Bank Sarasin.
The merger, if approved, would create an entity with combined managed assets of roughly 700 billion Swiss francs ($460 billion).
Roughly 100 billion francs of those assets will come from Winterthur, analysts said.
At a press briefing on Monday, Lukas Muehlemann, chief executive of Credit Suisse Group, said the merged group would be the third-largest asset manager for private and institutional investors.
It would trail only Fidelity Investments and AXA/UAP, the French-based firm which also has a roughly 60 percent stake in U.S. Equitable Cos Inc, and a large stake in Alliance Capital Management.

Winterthur, following the trend, is an investment house in its own right. In a report to shareholders in June, Winterthur said that on average that the group invested daily around 50 million Swiss francs worldwide.
While the amount under management is large, it is dwarfed in absolute terms by the global volme of pension fund assets.
Goldman Sachs estimates pension fund assets in the world's 15 largest countries will rise to $12 trillion by the end of the year 2000, from an estimated $7.4 trillion in 1995.
The trend is being fuelled in part by governments.

Frightened by a shift in demographics which according to worst-case estimates, leave, for example, only one legal worker per pension paid in Italy, European governments are seeking to encourage private sector retirement savings.
The potential is seen as large. Analyst Hans Kaufmann at Bank Julius Baer estimates only about 25 percent of Europeans are currently in a pension fund.
Opportunity is especially great in the countries with the lowest levels of pension fund assets relative to GDP such as France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Austria and Belgium.
Both banks and insurers are looking to combine forces to take advantage of the trend.

"Given the amount of pension reform we expect to take place in Europe, we think there are significant benefits there in terms of going into large corporations and helping them solve their pension or employee benefit problems, because most pension fund solutions involve both an insurance product and an asset management product," said Richard Thornburgh, chief financial officer of Credit Suisse Group, in an interview with Reuters Television.
The new Credit Suisse/Winterthur group, depending on the calculation, would derive between 20 and 27 percent of its pretax profit from insurance, according to Baer's Kaufmann.
The competition is growing as both fund managers and insurers vie for global economies of scale through international deals.
Zurich Group, Switzerland's largest insurer based on total premiums, bought U.S. asset manager Scudder, Stevens & Clark in June.

The world's largest fund manager, U.S.-based Fidelity Investments with $580 billion under management, is also strengthening its presence in Europe, planning to enter Spain next, according to a spokeswoman for the investment firm's Luxemborg-based unit.
Fidelity is already present in eight European countries, and wants to have a presence in all major Western European countries by the year 2000.
On the other side, insurers also have a huge stake in the market.
AXA/UAP in Paris, with $500 billion under management at the end of last year, said the concern is reassessing its asset management activities after it was formed through a recent merger itself.

"What we see is that asset management for us is closely related to our insurance business. Through life insurance, we are responsible for a large amount of money which is given to us by our insurance customers," an AXA/UAP spokesman said.

"Through the years we have developed a large expertise in asset management and we believe in developing worldwide this activity to put this expertise at the disposal of third parties, so we can sell asset management expertise," he said.
"We are reorganising all our asset activities Europe-wide," he said.
